questions.question: In story S6 (sendGroupRumor helper and own-send lifecycle), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/send/index.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/send/sendGroupRumor.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/send/ownRowTracker.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/send/groupOpQueue.ts; app/src/lib/pendingOwnSends.ts (re-pointed); app/tests/unit/marmot/send/*.test.ts and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `send` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S6 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S6's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/send/index.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/send/sendGroupRumor.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/send/ownRowTracker.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/send/groupOpQueue.ts; app/src/lib/pendingOwnSends.ts (re-pointed); app/tests/unit/marmot/send/*.test.ts)? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S6 implementation match the intent of its scope (send/ module: sendGroupRumor(group, kind, content, tags) (getEventHash id, own pubkey, group.send), serialised group.invite with group.synced() before commits and commit-pending retry, optimistic-row confirmation by rumor.id for either arrival order, and the four failure triggers (send reject, inten) and respect its exclusions (Migrating call sites (S18); Deleting sendRumorSafe copies (S22))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S6 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

Seam contract SendGroupRumor (consumed beyond S6; consumers: S18): does the delivered artifact at app/src/lib/marmot/send/sendGroupRumor.ts expose exactly the declared shape (fields: sendGroupRumor: (group: MarmotGroup, kind: number, content: string, tags: string[][]) => Promise<{id: string; result: unknown}>) and uphold each invariant (rumor id === getEventHash(rumor) and equals the id seen in the sink echo; pubkey is the own account; group.send called exactly once per call; no retry in the helper)? Show the type/definition with file:line and a test asserting each invariant, including enum/constant membership and value ranges where the contract constrains them.

Seam contract GroupOpQueue (consumed beyond S6; consumers: S8): does the delivered artifact at app/src/lib/marmot/send/groupOpQueue.ts expose exactly the declared shape (fields: run: <T>(groupId: string, op: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>) and uphold each invariant (at most one invite in flight per group; group.synced() awaited before invite/removeMember/setAdmins/rename/leave; commit-pending is retried after synced())? Show the type/definition with file:line and a test asserting each invariant, including enum/constant membership and value ranges where the contract constrains them.

AC-SEND-1: `sendGroupRumor(group, kind, content, tags)` MUST compute the rumor `id` with nostr-tools `getEventHash`, set `pubkey` to the own account, and call `group.send({type:'application', rumor})` exactly once with that rumor; the returned/optimistic id MUST equal the rumor id. For chat, the precomputed canonical id (AC-AR-21) MUST equal the id seen in the echoed sink entry. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-SEND-2: A harness send while a staged proposal is pending MUST deliver after the proposal commits with no app-side retry code; the second member receives the rumor with the identical id. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-SEND-5: At most one `group.invite` is in flight per group, and `group.synced()` is awaited before invite, removeMember, setAdmins, rename and leave. A test issuing two concurrent invites on one group MUST show serialisation (second call starts after first settles); a commit-pending rejection from a stub MUST be retried after `synced()`. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-OWN-1: Harness/unit: after a member sends a chat message through the send helper and the sink echo arrives, the chat store MUST contain exactly one row with that `rumor.id`, and the group's unread count and the bell counter MUST be unchanged from before the send. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [harness + unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-OWN-2: The own-echo path MUST hold for either arrival order: echo before `send()` resolves, and echo after. Both orders yield one row, status confirmed. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-WDR-3: Failure detection, one test per trigger: (a) `send()` rejects → row failed/retry; (b) `intentFailed` naming the row's group while unconfirmed → failed/retry; (c) `groupBranchSwitched` for the group while unconfirmed → failed/retry; (d) still unconfirmed 60 s (fake-time) after `send()` resolved → failed/retry. For a row already confirmed through the sink, none of (a)–(d) MUST change its status. A later sink arrival with the same `rumor.id` for a failed row MUST flip it to confirmed. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit (fake timers)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

The tracker's onOwnEcho/onOwnWithdrawn take an OPTIONAL third `eventId` (the kind-445 carrier) so a withdraw of one carrier does not fail a row another carrier confirmed (ownership-ledger S4 note), but the production handler ports (chatHandler.ts OwnEcho/OwnWithdrawn dep types and their call sites in createChatGroupHandler) still pass only (groupId, rumorId). Confirm: (a) the carrier logic is exercised in ownRowTracker.test.ts ('onOwnWithdrawn ignores a row confirmed by a DIFFERENT eventId'), (b) without an eventId a withdraw applies (the documented fallback), and (c) S18 or a follow-up must widen the handler ports to pass input.eventId for the carrier rule to be live in production; state whether leaving it unwired is acceptable for this story.

groupOpQueue chains ALL commit ops of one group and awaits group.synced() with no timeout. Show (groupOpQueue.ts runCommit) that a rejection never poisons the chain (test 'a failed first op does not stall or poison the second') and discuss the residual: a synced() that never settles (offline) blocks every later op of that group, including leave. Confirm the callers (S13 leave with leaveTimeoutMs, S14 admin ops) bound their own wait and that the queue is never entered from inside a library frame (it does not touch the client; frames must schedule through handle.enqueue).

Own optimistic poll votes / edits / deletes not yet echoed are reset by a recompute of their poll/slot (ledger S5 note). S6 chose: the tracker keeps the signal rumor while the row is `sending` and exposes pendingSignals(groupId) for the recompute caller to re-apply after the fold; failed or withdrawn signals are dropped (AC-WDR-2). Verify the accessor and its tests (ownRowTracker.test.ts 'own optimistic signals still sending ...', sendGroupRumor.test.ts), and that no recompute caller consumes it yet (S18 wiring): is any in-scope behaviour left unimplemented?

The A3 second-half harness (send.harness.test.ts) stages an abandoned send with a same-epoch fork and an outbound publish hold, then rejects the held publish. Observed library behaviour: while the publish is held the group's operation queue is blocked and the fork does not resolve; the app-visible signal is the send() rejection `publish-failed` (trigger a) -- the library emitted neither intentFailed nor groupBranchSwitched, nothing reached the sink, and the intent stays in group.pendingIntents(). Verify the assertions (no append on either sink, no withdraw, relay never stores the held event, row failed, group.send once) fail if the tracker's sendRejected is a no-op (mutation run recorded), and state the residual: a later publish of that pending intent would arrive as a sink echo and flip the row to confirmed (tracker-level covered, not end-to-end).

The own-row key is (groupId, rumor.id) and rumor.id = getEventHash of (pubkey, created_at seconds, kind, tags, content): two identical messages sent in the same second share one id, so the second prepare() re-registers a known row (no-op) and the library/sink see one logical rumor. Confirm this matches the pre-adoption behaviour (buildChatRumor had the same id basis), whether S18 must add a uniqueness tag, and that the helper never reuses an id across different content.

pendingOwnSendsStatusPort maps failed -> settlePendingOwnSend(owner, id, false), which forgets the pending entry (module-scope pendingOwnSends semantics are preserved: per-owner keys, remount catch-up via settle listeners). Show that the port tolerates unknown rows (no throw), that the tracker swallows a throwing port (console.warn, lifecycle continues), and that nothing in send/ imports React, idb-keyval or the stores (status goes out through the injected port only).
